title: Consignment visibility, without the chase
summary: A read-only visibility pilot that helps the service team identify and resolve shipment exceptions.
goals: Reduce time spent reconciling consignment status across three systems.
Help service agents spot delayed or contradictory shipment updates sooner.
Give the sponsor evidence to decide whether wider automation is worthwhile.
inScope: Read-only status ingestion from up to three agreed systems.
A reconciled consignment view with source timestamps and exception flags.
Draft exception messages for service-agent approval.
A pilot with one service team and an agreed shipment cohort.
outOfScope: Replacing transport or warehouse management systems.
Autonomous customer messaging or changes to shipment instructions.
Predictive arrival guarantees or a full customer tracking portal.

assumptions.text: Three source systems expose usable read-only extracts or APIs.
A service manager can nominate pilot users and a baseline.
The first pilot can operate without a new customer-facing portal.

questions.question: Who owns the budget, and what decision will a successful pilot unlock?
questions.why: Sets the pilot investment ceiling and avoids an unfunded rollout.

questions.question: Do all three systems share a reliable consignment identifier?
questions.why: Identity matching may dominate integration effort.

questions.question: Who approves exception messages, and how quickly?
questions.why: Human approval capacity determines the achievable response time.

questions.question: What shipment or contact data can leave the source systems?
questions.why: Defines retention, hosting and redaction requirements.

phases.name: Discover
phases.objective: Confirm source access, consignment identity and the service-team baseline.
activities: Interview the sponsor and nominated pilot users.
Profile approved sample data and identify access gaps.
Agree baseline measures, acceptance thresholds and a go/no-go gate.
phases.exitCriteria: Sponsor signs off the pilot boundary, data access and evaluation plan.

phases.name: Design
phases.objective: Turn agreed outcomes and controls into a buildable pilot design.
activities: Map the bounded workflow and reviewer responsibilities.
Define interfaces, failure handling and evidence requirements.
Review the design with the operational and compliance owners.
phases.exitCriteria: Design and required control owners approve the implementation plan.

phases.name: Build
phases.objective: Implement source mapping, status reconciliation and an approval queue.
activities: Implement only the agreed data inputs and workflow.
Add traceability, access controls and explicit failure states.
Evaluate representative and adversarial cases against the reference set.
phases.exitCriteria: The test cohort meets agreed quality thresholds; critical issues are resolved.

phases.name: Pilot
phases.objective: Evaluate usefulness and reliability with the agreed user cohort.
activities: Onboard pilot users and train reviewers.
Run a bounded trial against the baseline.
Capture errors, review effort and user feedback.
phases.exitCriteria: Sponsor reviews measured results and decides to stop, iterate or expand.

phases.name: Handover
phases.objective: Give the owner a controlled, maintainable next step.
activities: Document the workflow, limits and operational runbook.
Present the pilot findings and a separately scoped rollout option.
phases.exitCriteria: Named owner accepts the handover and the next-step decision is recorded.

drivers.detail: Up to 3 source systems; connectors and identifier mapping.
Identifier quality and timestamp consistency are unverified.
Service agents approve every draft exception message.

risks.mitigation: Display source and freshness; route conflicts to manual review.
Keep all messages in an approval queue during the pilot.

risks.risk: Integration access delays the quarter target.
risks.mitigation: Use approved sample extracts during discovery; gate build on access.

metrics.target: Proposed: 40% reduction against a two-week baseline.
Proposed: at least 90% on the agreed labelled cohort.
Proposed: 70% accepted with only minor edits.
